references.text: This also mentions an understanding of resurrection from the dead, which the disciples discussed in Mark 9:10.

This verse refers to Jesus and his disciples descending from the mountain after the transfiguration, where Jesus instructs them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man has risen from the dead, relating to the disciples' wonder in Mark 9:10.
In this passage, the Sadducees challenge Jesus with a question about the resurrection, which is relevant to the disciples' discussion in Mark 9:10.
Similar to Matthew 22:23-33, here the Sadducees challenge Jesus regarding the resurrection, providing background to the disciples' wonder in Mark 9:10.

The Acts of the Apostles describes how Peter and John were arrested for teaching the people and proclaiming the resurrection from the dead in Jesus, which provides context to the disciples' question in Mark 9:10.
Paul's preaching in Athens about Jesus and the resurrection arouses curiosity among the philosophers, reflecting the early Christian church's focus on the resurrection, related to Mark 9:10.
Paul uses his belief in the resurrection as a defense point before the Sanhedrin, underscoring the importance of faith in the resurrection, which also puzzled the disciples in Mark 9:10.

Paul's defense for his faith includes an affirmation of hope in the resurrection, both for the righteous and the unrighteous, offering insight into the early Christian understanding of the resurrection discussed in Mark 9:10.
Paul's extensive teaching on the resurrection in 1 Corinthians provides theological background to the disciples' question in Mark 9:10.
